flags.sentence: But even if the company’s forecast appears beside that line, we cannot say, “AI demand is strong, so revenue will be about $34.8 billion.” This announcement alone does not explain how the two are connected.
flags.question: 文中の「This announcement alone does not explain how the two are connected」は、台帳の「連結売上高見通し」と「CEOによる需要評価」からは確認できない、発表内に両者の関連説明がないという断定ではありませんか。

sentences.s1: # AI Is the Star, but the Trailer Is for the Whole Company!
sentences.s2: The “Cast” of Numbers in Broadcom’s Earnings
sentences.s3: “AI semiconductor revenue: $16.7 billion!” If that number fills the screen, you hear a fanfare in your head.
sentences.s4: The star, AI, seems to have pulled off another big job.
sentences.s5: Then the words “Next: about $34.8 billion” appear.
sentences.s6: Wow, is the sequel suddenly going to be much bigger?
sentences.s8: Has this edit joined two different numbers?
sentences.s9: Broadcom’s earnings report is much easier to follow if we check the “cast” of the numbers.
sentences.s10: Revenue for the company as a whole was $29.591 billion.
sentences.s11: That is the result for the whole company.
sentences.s12: By contrast, $16.7 billion was revenue from AI semiconductors.
sentences.s13: Even though both appear in the same announcement, they show different things—like a group photo of the entire cast and a close-up of the star.
sentences.s15: It is the company’s forecast for its total revenue in the next quarter.
sentences.s16: In other words, what is being previewed is the whole company next time, not the future of AI semiconductors alone.
sentences.s17: If a caption said, “AI revenue rises from $16.7 billion to $34.8 billion!”, that would not be the company’s announcement.
sentences.s18: It would be an overly bold re-edit by the audience.
sentences.s19: Now let’s sort out the cast list.
sentences.s20: $16.7 billion is “AI semiconductor results.” $29.591 billion is “whole-company results.” About $34.8 billion is “whole-company forecast.” “AI or the whole company?” and “Actual results or a forecast?” If we remove these two labels, the earnings report quickly turns into a comedy of mix-ups.
sentences.s21: Of course, AI does get its big moment.
sentences.s22: The CEO said that demand for custom AI accelerators and networking remains very strong.
sentences.s23: It is a strong line that gives a sense of the star’s momentum.
sentences.s24: We should listen to it as it is.
sentences.s25: But even if the company’s forecast appears beside that line, we cannot say, “AI demand is strong, so revenue will be about $34.8 billion.” This announcement alone does not explain how the two are connected.
sentences.s26: We should not see two scenes next to each other and make up the script in between.
sentences.s27: The key questions when looking at earnings are: “What is this number for?” and “Is it an actual result or a forecast?” Just these two questions are enough to clearly separate the star’s performance from the outlook for the whole production.
sentences.s29: But the sign for the next preview says “the whole company.” Let’s pause for a moment with the popcorn in hand and make sure we don’t miss that.
sentences.s31: Broadcom’s $34.8 billion forecast is for the whole company, not just AI semiconductors.

対象企業はBroadcom Inc.。同社は2026年9月2日、2026年度第3四半期の決算を発表した。
  scope: Broadcom Inc.の連結業績
  date_or_period: 2026年9月2日発表。2026年度第3四半期（2026年8月2日終了）
  ambiguity_note: Broadcomが2026年9月2日に2026年度第3四半期（2026年8月2日終了）の決算を発表したことは確認できました。ただし、対象テーマの「最も最近の発表」という選定条件は、Broadcomの発表日だけでは確認できません。たとえば「leading AI chipmaker」にAI向けメモリのMicronも含めるなら、同社は9月30日にFY2026第4四半期の決算を発表しており、Broadcomより後です。分類の範囲が曖昧なため、Broadcomを選定対象とする前提は確定できません。([investors.broadcom.com](https://investors.broadcom.com/news-releases/news-release-details/broadcom-inc-announces-third-quarter-fiscal-year-2026-financial))
